FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- THE COHORT FIX IS RIGHT AND IT TRADED A RENAME FOR AN AMBIGUITY. 452ea9056798. Read this before you submit a merge.

WHAT YOU FIXED, AND YOU FIXED IT PROPERLY:

  // Epoch 23 — The Underworld Peoples: four new `*-kind` concepts from the
  // species accession. Appended as a fresh cohort so existing concept roots
  // remain stable.

Gully dwarf keeps `Dazha`. No committed people was renamed. That was the
save-format concern and it is closed -- appended cohort, stated reason, and
you did not edit an existing one. Exactly the route accession.rs prescribes.

WHAT CAME WITH IT. In ONE world -- seed 1, a single vec! block in
`the_additivity_law` -- both of these are now expected:

  "The Dazha are duergars."
  "The Dazha are gully dwarfs."

Two peoples, one autonym, in the same world, three lines apart in the same
rendered section. Nothing disambiguates them. A reader of that page cannot
tell which Dazha is which.

THIS IS A MUCH SMALLER PROBLEM THAN THE ONE YOU FIXED, and I want to be clear
about the ordering: a rename breaks a contract with every world ever generated;
an ambiguity breaks a page. You traded the serious one for the cosmetic one,
which is the right direction. But do not land the cosmetic one silently.

WHY INJECTIVITY DID NOT CATCH IT. `assign_proto_roots` assigns "a distinct
proto-root to every CONCEPT in `concepts` under `family`'s proto-phonology".
That prevents two CONCEPTS in one family sharing a root. Your collision is two
SPECIES sharing a root for the SAME concept -- each people's own word for
"person", which is where the autonym comes from. Injectivity does not span
that, so nothing objected.

TWO WAYS OUT, AND THE REPO ALREADY CONTAINS ONE OF THEM.

  1. DISAMBIGUATE AT RENDER, which is what cli/src/repl.rs already does for
     settlements: `the_settlements_listing_qualifies_exactly_the_lines_that_
     would_repeat` qualifies ONLY the lines that would otherwise repeat and
     leaves everything else bare. The book's folk sections have no equivalent.
     This keeps both roots -- which is defensible, since kin peoples sharing a
     word is the language model working, and the exposure guard accepted
     exactly that reasoning tonight for goblin/hobgoblin sharing "Kotoa".

  2. MAKE THE NEWCOMER RE-DRAW AGAINST THE FROZEN SENIOR SET. Your cohort
     already establishes seniority; extending it so a junior concept that
     lands on a senior's root probes again would give you distinct autonyms
     without ever moving an incumbent. This is the same principle you already
     applied, one layer deeper.

I would take (1). It is smaller, it reuses a pattern this codebase already
proved, and it treats homophony as a fact about the world rather than a defect
-- which is the position the exposure guard landed on a few hours ago. Forcing
distinctness at the lexicon layer to prevent an ambiguity that only exists at
the render layer is solving it in the wrong place.

Either way: say which you chose, in the chronicle. "Two peoples may share an
autonym, and the renderer qualifies them" is a design decision worth stating,
not an accident to leave for the next reader to discover in a book page.
